name: Char Kway Teow
blurb: Smoky wok-fried flat rice noodles with prawns, egg, chinese sausage and beansprouts.
ingredients: 400g fresh wide flat rice noodles (ho fun), loosened
1 tbsp dark soy, 2 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar
method: Mix the soy sauces, oyster sauce, sugar and chilli paste in a small bowl.
Get a wok scorching hot with 1 tbsp oil. Fry the sausage for 1 minute, add the garlic and prawns and stir-fry until the prawns just turn pink.
Push everything aside, add a splash more oil and the eggs, and scramble roughly.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss hard for 2 minutes, letting the noodles catch a little for smokiness.
Throw in the beansprouts and spring onions, toss 30 seconds so they stay crunchy, and serve at once.

name: Nasi Lemak
blurb: Fragrant coconut rice with a fiery sambal, crunchy peanuts, cucumber and a fried egg.
ingredients: 3 pandan leaves knotted (optional), 1 slice ginger, 1/2 tsp salt
For the sambal: 6 dried chillies soaked, 2 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp shrimp paste (optional), 1 tbsp tamarind, 1 tbsp sugar
Crispy fried shallots and lime, to serve
method: Cook the rice with the coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt — bring to a boil, cover, lowest heat 12 minutes, then rest 10.

Blitz the sambal chillies, shallots, garlic and shrimp paste to a paste. Fry in 3 tbsp oil over medium-low for 10-12 minutes until dark and split, then stir in the tamarind and sugar and cook to a jammy relish.
Fry the eggs with crispy lacy edges.
Fluff the rice and mound onto plates.
Add a spoon of sambal, a pile of peanuts, cucumber slices, an egg and a scatter of fried shallots, with lime to squeeze.

name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
blurb: Silky poached chicken with rice cooked in the poaching stock, and three punchy dipping sauces.
ingredients: 1 thumb ginger sliced, 4 spring onions, 6 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp salt
1 tbsp chicken fat or oil, 2 garlic cloves and 2cm ginger minced (for the rice)
Chilli sauce: 4 red chillies, 2 garlic cloves, 2cm ginger, 1 tbsp lime, pinch sugar, 3 tbsp stock — blitzed
Ginger-scallion: 4 tbsp minced ginger and 6 spring onions with 4 tbsp hot oil and a pinch of salt
Cucumber slices and coriander, to serve
method: Put the chicken in a snug pot with the ginger, spring onions, garlic and salt. Cover with cold water, bring just to a bare simmer, then poach very gently for 35-40 minutes (barely a bubble). Lift out and plunge into iced water for 5 minutes, then rub with a little sesame oil. Keep the stock.
Fry the minced garlic and ginger in the chicken fat, add the rinsed rice and toast 2 minutes, then cook with 480ml of the hot poaching stock — boil, cover, lowest heat 12 minutes, rest 10.
Make the chilli sauce and the ginger-scallion sauce.
Carve the chicken into pieces.
Serve the chicken over or beside the rice with a bowl of hot clear stock, cucumber, and the three sauces plus dark soy.

name: Chinese Takeaway Chicken Curry
blurb: That glossy, mild, slightly sweet chip-shop curry sauce over chicken, peas and onions with rice.
ingredients: Steamed rice or chips, to serve
method: Fry the onions in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until very soft and pale gold.
Stir in the curry powder, five-spice, turmeric and ginger and cook 1 minute, then the flour for another minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock, add the soy and sugar, and simmer for 10 minutes until smooth and glossy. Blitz for the classic silky texture if you like.
Add the chicken and peas and simmer for 6-8 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce coats a spoon.
Serve over rice or with chips.

name: Hot & Sour Soup
blurb: A peppery, vinegar-sharp broth thick with tofu, mushrooms, bamboo and ribbons of egg.
ingredients: 150g firm tofu, cut into thin batons
1 small tin bamboo shoots, drained and shredded
1 tbsp chilli oil or chilli bean paste
3 tbsp cornflour mixed with 5 tbsp water
2 eggs, beaten; 2 spring onions and 1 tsp sesame oil, to finish
method: Bring the stock to a simmer with the mushrooms and bamboo shoots and cook 5 minutes.
Add the tofu, soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper and chilli oil.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and simmer 2 minutes until the soup thickens to a light gravy.
Turn off the heat. Pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream while stirring gently so it sets in ribbons.
Taste and add more vinegar or pepper — it should make you sniff. Finish with spring onions and sesame oil.

name: Egg Foo Young
blurb: Fluffy Cantonese omelettes packed with prawns and vegetables under a glossy brown gravy.
ingredients: 150g cooked small prawns or shredded char siu
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil (for the egg)
For the gravy: 300ml chicken stock, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp cornflour slaked in water
method: Simmer the gravy ingredients (except cornflour) for 2 minutes, then stir in the slaked cornflour and cook to a glossy sauce. Keep warm.
Mix the beaten eggs with the prawns, beansprouts, spring onions, water chestnuts, soy and sesame oil.
Heat a good slick of oil in a small frying pan over medium-high. Ladle in about a quarter of the mixture and fry for 2 minutes until golden underneath, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
Repeat for the rest, keeping the omelettes warm.
Serve on rice with the hot gravy poured over.

name: Beef Chow Fun
blurb: Wide rice noodles and marinated beef seared hard in a smoky, dark-soy wok toss with beansprouts.
ingredients: 250g rump or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
1 tsp cornflour, 1 tsp soy, 1 tsp shaoxing wine (to marinate)
400g fresh wide flat rice noodles, loosened
1 tbsp dark soy, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp sugar
method: Toss the beef with the cornflour, soy and wine and leave 10 minutes.
Get a wok smoking hot with 1 tbsp oil. Sear the beef in one layer for 1 minute without moving, then toss for 30 seconds and tip out.
Add a little more oil and the garlic, then the noodles. Add the dark and light soy and sugar and toss gently but firmly for 2 minutes, letting the noodles catch.
Return the beef with the beansprouts and spring onions and toss for 30 seconds.
Serve straight from the wok.

name: Pork Sinigang
blurb: A bright, sour Filipino tamarind broth with pork ribs, daikon, green beans and water spinach.
ingredients: 800g pork ribs or belly, in chunks
1 bunch water spinach or spinach, chopped
Fish sauce, to season; steamed rice, to serve
method: Put the pork, onion and tomatoes in a pot with the water. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 45 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the tamarind paste until dissolved and the broth turns properly sour — add more to taste.
Add the daikon and simmer 8 minutes, then the aubergine, beans and whole chillies for 5 minutes.
Stir in the greens and cook 1 minute until just wilted.
Season with fish sauce — it should be sour first, salty second. Serve in bowls with rice.

name: Kare-Kare
blurb: Filipino oxtail and vegetables in a thick, mild peanut and toasted-rice sauce, with salty shrimp paste on the side.
ingredients: 80g smooth peanut butter, plus 40g ground roasted peanuts
3 tbsp raw rice, toasted and ground to a powder
2 tbsp annatto seeds steeped in 4 tbsp hot oil (or 1 tsp paprika)
1 aubergine sliced, 150g green beans, 1 bundle pak choi or banana heart
method: Simmer the oxtail with the onion and garlic in water to cover for 2.5-3 hours until very tender. Keep 1 litre of the stock.
Strain the annatto oil into a wide pan and warm it. Whisk in the peanut butter, ground peanuts and toasted rice powder, then the reserved stock, and simmer to a thick, smooth gravy.
Add the oxtail and season with the fish sauce.
Blanch or fry the aubergine, beans and greens separately until just tender and add to the pot to warm through.
Serve with rice and a small dish of shrimp paste to stir in bite by bite.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Grilled Chicken
blurb: Chicken thighs marinated in lemongrass, garlic and fish sauce, charred and served with rice and pickles.
ingredients: Steamed rice, sliced cucumber and quick carrot pickle, to serve
Nuoc cham (fish sauce, lime, sugar, garlic, chilli, water), to drizzle
method: Blitz or pound the lemongrass, garlic, shallots, fish sauce, sugar, oil, soy and chilli to a loose paste.
Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 20 minutes (or overnight).
Grill, griddle or barbecue over a medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes each side until caramelised at the edges and cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Serve over rice with cucumber, carrot pickle and a good spoon of nuoc cham.

name: Chicken Cacciatore
blurb: Hunter's-style chicken braised with tomatoes, peppers, olives, rosemary and a splash of red wine.
ingredients: 80g black olives, sprig of rosemary, 1 bay leaf
Polenta, potatoes or crusty bread, to serve
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down in a wide pan until deep gold, turn briefly, then lift out.
Fry the onion and peppers in the fat for 8 minutes, add the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, stock, olives, rosemary and bay.
Return the chicken skin-side up and simmer uncovered for 30-35 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken tender.
Discard the rosemary and bay and serve with polenta or potatoes.

name: Chicken Milanese
blurb: Thin breaded chicken fried crisp and golden, served with a lemon-dressed rocket and tomato salad.
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts, butterflied and beaten to 5mm
150g fine dried breadcrumbs mixed with 30g grated Parmesan
Olive oil and 30g butter, for frying
Lemon, extra virgin olive oil, to dress
method: Season the chicken, then coat each piece in flour, then egg, then the Parmesan breadcrumbs, pressing them on firmly.
Heat a 3mm depth of olive oil with the butter in a large pan over medium-high.
Fry the escalopes for 3 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack and salt lightly.
Toss the rocket, tomatoes and onion with lemon juice, olive oil and seasoning.
Serve each escalope topped with a handful of the salad and lemon wedges.

name: Pasta e Fagioli
blurb: A thick, humble Italian soup-stew of borlotti beans, small pasta, tomato and rosemary.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins borlotti or cannellini beans
1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, finely diced
1 sprig rosemary, 1 bay leaf, pinch chilli flakes
Parmesan rind (optional), plus grated Parmesan to serve
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in 3 tbsp olive oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato purée, rosemary, bay and chilli for 2 minutes.
Add one tin of beans with their liquid and roughly mash, then add the second tin drained, the stock and the Parmesan rind.
Simmer for 15 minutes, then add the pasta and cook until al dente, adding water if it gets too thick — it should be spoonable, not soupy.
Discard the rosemary, bay and rind. Season well.
Serve with a hard grating of Parmesan and a generous swirl of olive oil.

name: Ham & Ricotta Calzone
blurb: A folded, stuffed pizza — molten ricotta, mozzarella and ham inside a puffed, blistered crust.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (300g strong flour, 1/2 tsp yeast, 1 tsp salt, 200ml warm water, 1 tbsp oil), proved and divided into 4
Handful of basil, grating of nutmeg
Simple tomato sauce (400g passata simmered with garlic and oregano), to serve
method: Heat the oven with a heavy tray inside to its maximum for 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, half the mozzarella, the Parmesan, nutmeg and seasoning.
Stretch each dough ball to a 22cm round. Spread the ricotta mix over one half, top with ham, the rest of the mozzarella and torn basil, leaving a border.
Fold over into a half-moon, press and crimp the edge firmly, and cut two small steam vents. Glaze with egg.
Bake on the hot tray for 10-12 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Serve with the warm tomato sauce for dipping.

name: Pasta alla Gricia
blurb: The ancestor of amatriciana without the tomato: crisp guanciale, pecorino and a storm of black pepper.
ingredients: 150g guanciale (or pancetta), cut into short lardons
method: Put the pasta on to cook in well-salted water.
Fry the guanciale in a cold dry pan, bringing it up to medium heat, until the fat has rendered and the pieces are golden and crisp. Take off the heat and keep the fat.
Toast the black pepper in the guanciale fat for a few seconds, then add a ladle of pasta water and swirl.
Drain the pasta a minute early and add it to the pan with the guanciale. Toss over low heat, adding pasta water bit by bit.
Off the heat, add the pecorino a handful at a time, tossing hard, until you have a creamy, clinging sauce. Serve at once with more pepper.

name: Chilaquiles Rojos with Fried Eggs
blurb: Tortilla chips simmered briefly in a smoky red salsa so they soften at the edges but keep some bite, topped with egg, crema and onion.
ingredients: 200g lightly salted tortilla chips (or fry 6 corn tortillas cut into triangles)
4 tomatoes and 2 dried chipotle or ancho chillies (soaked), or 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo
Crema or soured cream, sliced red onion, coriander
method: Blitz the tomatoes, chillies, onion and garlic to a smooth salsa.
Fry the salsa in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until darkened, then add the stock and simmer to a loose, pourable sauce. Season.
Fry the eggs to your liking in a separate pan.
Add the tortilla chips to the simmering sauce and fold gently for 1-2 minutes — you want them coated and softening but not turned to mush.
Tip onto plates, top with the eggs, then crema, cheese, red onion and coriander, with lime to squeeze.

name: Camarones a la Diabla
blurb: Prawns in a fiery, brick-red sauce of guajillo and chipotle chillies, garlic and tomato.
ingredients: 4 guajillo chillies and 2 chipotles (or 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo), stemmed and soaked
Lime, coriander and steamed rice, to serve
method: Blitz the soaked chillies, tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano, cumin and tomato purée with the stock to a smooth sauce.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the sauce for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens.
Season the prawns and add them to the sauce.
Cook for 3-4 minutes, turning, just until the prawns are pink and firm.
Finish with lime juice and coriander and serve with rice to soak up the sauce.

name: Rajas con Crema Tacos
blurb: Charred poblano strips softened with onion and sweetcorn in a light cream sauce, folded into warm tortillas.
method: Blister the poblanos directly over a flame or under a hot grill until blackened all over. Steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then rub off the skins, deseed and slice into strips (rajas).
Fry the onions in a little oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the pepper strips, sweetcorn and oregano and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the crema and milk and simmer 3-4 minutes to a loose sauce. Season and add most of the cheese.
Spoon into warm tortillas, top with the rest of the cheese and serve with lime.

name: Enchiladas Suizas
blurb: Chicken-filled tortillas under a tangy green tomatillo sauce and a blanket of melted cheese.
ingredients: 600g tomatillos (or 2 tins), or 500g green tomatoes + 2 tbsp lime
2 green chillies, 1/2 onion, 2 garlic cloves, small bunch coriander
200g grated cheese (Monterey Jack or mild cheddar)
Sliced onion and coriander, to serve
method: Simmer the tomatillos, chillies, onion and garlic in a little water for 8 minutes until soft, then blitz with the coriander, stock and cream to a smooth pourable sauce. Season.
Warm each tortilla briefly in a little oil so it is pliable.
Fill each with shredded chicken, roll up and pack seam-down into a baking dish.
Pour over all the sauce so the tortillas are covered, then scatter with the cheese.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden. Top with raw onion and coriander to serve.

name: Brazilian Feijoada
blurb: A deep, smoky black bean stew with several cuts of pork and beef, served with rice, greens and orange.
ingredients: For the couve: 1 bunch spring greens or kale, finely shredded, fried with garlic
Steamed rice, orange segments and hot sauce, to serve
method: Brown all the meats in a large pot in batches, then set aside. Soften the onions and garlic in the fat for 10 minutes with the cumin.
Return the meats, add the drained beans and bay, and cover with water by 5cm.
Simmer gently, part-covered, for about 2 hours until the beans are creamy and the meat is tender, topping up with water as needed.
Lift out the meats, slice, and stir the sliced sausage and larger pieces back in. Mash a ladle of beans against the side to thicken the pot.
Fry the shredded greens hard with garlic. Serve the feijoada with rice, the greens, a few orange segments and hot sauce.

name: Lomo Saltado
blurb: Peruvian stir-fry of beef, onion and tomato in soy and vinegar, piled with chips and served with rice.
ingredients: 600g sirloin or rump steak, cut into thick strips
1 aji amarillo or 1 yellow chilli, sliced
method: Season the beef well and sear it in two batches in a screaming-hot wok or heavy pan for 1-2 minutes so it browns but stays pink inside. Set aside.
Add the onions and chilli to the pan and stir-fry for 2 minutes so they keep some crunch, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and toss for 1 minute.
Return the beef, add the soy and vinegar and toss for 30 seconds, scraping up the pan.
Fold through the hot chips and the coriander and serve straight away, with rice on the side.

name: Moqueca
blurb: A vivid Brazilian fish stew in coconut milk, tomatoes and peppers, finished with lime and dendê oil.
ingredients: 700g firm white fish (cod, hake or monkfish), in large chunks
Juice of 2 limes, 3 garlic cloves crushed (to marinate)
2 tbsp palm (dendê) oil or olive oil
method: Toss the fish with the lime juice, garlic and a little salt and leave for 15 minutes.
In a wide pan or clay pot, layer half the onions, peppers and tomatoes. Sit the fish (and prawns) on top, then the rest of the vegetables. Add the paprika and chilli.
Pour over the coconut milk and dendê oil, bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 15-18 minutes without stirring much, so the fish stays whole.
Scatter over most of the coriander and simmer 2 minutes more.
Check for lime and salt and serve straight from the pot with rice.

name: Pav Bhaji
blurb: Mumbai street food: a spiced, buttery mash of mixed vegetables scooped up with griddled buttered rolls.
ingredients: 3 potatoes, 1 small cauliflower, 150g peas, 1 carrot — all boiled soft
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp chilli powder
80g butter, plus extra for the pav
1 red onion diced, coriander and lemon wedges, to serve
method: Melt half the butter and fry the onions until soft, add the ginger-garlic paste and pepper for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook down to a paste, then stir in the pav bhaji masala and chilli powder for 1 minute.
Add all the boiled vegetables with a splash of their water and mash directly in the pan to a coarse, spreadable bhaji. Simmer 10 minutes, stirring, adding water to loosen.
Beat in the rest of the butter until glossy. Season with salt and lemon.
Split the rolls, griddle them cut-side down in butter until golden, and serve alongside the bhaji topped with raw onion, coriander and lemon.

name: Anda Bhurji
blurb: Indian-style spiced scrambled eggs with onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander, for toast or roti.
ingredients: 6 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp garam masala
Buttered toast, roti or pav, to serve
method: Heat the oil and crackle the cumin seeds. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the ginger and chillies for 1 minute, then the tomato and turmeric and cook 2 minutes to a paste.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir over medium-low heat, folding, until just set and still soft.
Stir through the garam masala and most of the coriander.
Serve piled onto buttered toast or with warm roti, scattered with the rest of the coriander.

name: Chicken Pathia
blurb: A British curry-house favourite: hot, sweet and sour all at once, with tamarind and a touch of sugar.
ingredients: 3 tbsp medium curry paste (or 2 tbsp curry powder)
1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp fenugreek
method: Fry the onions in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat for 12 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then the curry paste, chilli powder, paprika and fenugreek and cook out for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer 5 minutes, then blitz smooth for a classic curry-house texture if you like.
Add the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the tamarind and sugar, balance to taste so it is hot then sweet then sharp, and serve with coriander and rice.

name: Kadhi Pakora
blurb: Silky, tangy gram-flour and yoghurt curry with soft onion fritters bobbing in it, over rice.
ingredients: For the pakora: 120g gram (chickpea) flour, 2 onions thinly sliced, 1 green chilli, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli, pinch bicarb, water to bind
For the kadhi: 60g gram flour, 400g natural yoghurt, 1.2 litres water
Tempering: 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 10 curry leaves, 2 dried chillies, pinch asafoetida
method: Mix the pakora ingredients to a thick, dropping batter. Fry heaped teaspoons in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden. Drain.
Whisk the gram flour into the yoghurt until smooth, then whisk in the water, turmeric, chilli powder and ginger-garlic paste.
Pour into a pot and bring to a simmer, whisking, then cook on low for 20-25 minutes, stirring often, until thickened and no longer raw-tasting.
Slip in the pakoras and simmer 5 minutes so they soak up the kadhi.
Heat the ghee and fry the tempering spices until they pop and the curry leaves crackle, then pour it sizzling over the kadhi. Serve with rice.

name: Maqluba
blurb: A Levantine 'upside-down' pot of spiced rice, chicken and fried aubergine, flipped out at the table.
ingredients: 2 onions, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom pods, 2 bay leaves
2 tbsp baharat or maqluba spice mix
500g basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
Toasted pine nuts and almonds, chopped parsley, to finish
Cucumber and yoghurt salad, to serve
method: Simmer the chicken with 1 onion, the whole spices and 1 tbsp baharat in water to cover for 30 minutes. Lift out the chicken; strain and keep 900ml of the stock.
Fry the aubergine and cauliflower in batches until golden; drain.

Rub a wide, heavy pot with oil. Arrange the chicken over the base, then layers of aubergine and cauliflower, then the drained rice mixed with the rest of the baharat and a sliced onion. Press down gently.
Pour the hot stock down the side to just cover the rice. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes. Rest, covered, for 15 minutes.
Put a large platter over the pot and, with confidence, invert it. Lift the pot away, scatter with nuts and parsley, and serve with the yoghurt salad.

name: Misir Wot
blurb: Ethiopian red lentils stewed low with berbere and caramelised onion into a rich, spicy purée.
ingredients: 3 tbsp oil (or niter kibbeh for the classic flavour)
4 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, grated
method: Cook the onions in a dry pan over low heat, stirring often, for 12-15 minutes until deeply softened and starting to colour.
Add the oil, garlic and ginger and cook 3 minutes, then stir in the berbere and tomato purée and fry gently for 2-3 minutes until dark and fragrant.
Add the lentils and water, bring to a simmer and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick, spoonable stew.
Season with salt and loosen with a little water if needed.
Serve with injera or flatbread to scoop, ideally with a cooling side of chopped tomato and onion salad.

name: Suya Skewers
blurb: West African street skewers of thin beef rubbed in a spiced peanut 'yaji' and grilled over high heat.
ingredients: 600g sirloin or rump steak, sliced thin

For the yaji: 60g roasted peanuts blitzed to a coarse powder, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp ground ginger, 1 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp garlic granules, 1 tsp onion granules, 1 stock cube crushed, 1/2 tsp salt
Flatbreads and lime wedges, to serve
method: Mix all the yaji ingredients. Reserve a third for dusting at the end.
Toss the beef with the oil and two-thirds of the yaji and leave 15 minutes.
Thread the beef onto skewers in loose folds.
Grill, griddle or barbecue over a high heat for 2 minutes each side until charred at the edges but still juicy.
Dust with the reserved yaji straight off the heat and serve with sliced onion, tomato, flatbreads and lime.

name: Coronation Chicken
blurb: Poached chicken in a lightly curried, apricot-sweet mayonnaise with almonds — for a plate or a jacket.
ingredients: 600g cooked chicken, shredded (or poach 4 breasts and cool)
2 tbsp apricot jam or mango chutney
Rice salad or baked potatoes and dressed leaves, to serve
method: Warm the curry powder in a dry pan for 30 seconds until fragrant, then let it cool.
Whisk the mayonnaise, yoghurt, curry powder, apricot jam, tomato purée and lemon into a smooth, glossy dressing. Loosen with a little water if thick.
Fold in the chicken, sultanas and most of the almonds and season.
Chill for 20 minutes for the flavours to settle.
Serve over a rice salad or with baked potatoes and leaves, scattered with the rest of the almonds.
